rapport_notes: Warm, conversational tone; genuine interest in customer's situation (divorce context); empathetic comments ('I know, I feel'); natural banter about motorized couches.
process_discipline_notes: The rep delivered the estimate anchor, then later asked 'Anything else that I can answer for you today?' but did not hold silence afterward before launching into packing upsell—customer raised a new question, but the pattern shows no deliberate pause/silence discipline.

evidence_quotes.agenda: And then, do you have any specific questions or concerns about this move? [Asked after substantial logistics probing had already begun — callback information, dates, name, email, pickup address, square footage, bedrooms, parking distance, box count, furniture inventory, delivery address, square footage, stories, bedrooms had all been gathered first.]
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Rep asked about TV concern: 'Yeah, we definitely. We'll take them down, we just can't, reinstall so that would work as well, if that's what they wanted to do.' Customer then volunteered additional context ('Okay, okay, that'd be 144. Sorry, go ahead.'), and rep pivoted naturally without re-probing, which is acceptable because the customer signaled completion. The concern was adequately explored and resolved.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: Commit to rate: 'Everything is included in that hourly rate. So the gas and truck taxes, insurance, all rap pads and band protect items from being moved. All tools for disassemble and reassembly. A. Furniture and appliances.' | Estimate is a window: 'obviously their number of factors involved when determining move time but the most important one is how well prepared you are, when we get there.' | Beats it pay less: 'the time is pro rated in fifteen minute increments' | Self-prep tip: 'You're taking this small things over yourself and a car loader too so that really helps keep the time down in our efficiency up. Obviously less time we take. Less money end up spending at the end of the day.' | No silence after 'does that feel fair' — that line was never asked.

top_strength: Brianne expertly gathered comprehensive logistics detail (furniture inventory, room-by-room layout, distances, square footage, delivery address) and proactively ordered a truck with a lift gate without charging extra, demonstrating attentiveness to the customer's needs and efficiency mindset.
coaching_note: Add the quid-pro-quo framing at the very beginning ('Let me grab a few details to build you an accurate quote, should take about six minutes') and always ask the agenda line before pulling logistics; also use deliberate silence after open-ended questions like 'does that feel fair' and the final 'anything else' to let the customer think and respond naturally, rather than filling the pause.
